subtitle: When cannon kept their silence, an empire lost its voice

panels.shot: epic bird's-eye over the Ganges plain, two distant armies facing, a dark line of silent cannon between them
panels.action: On the sun-bleached plain by the Ganges near Kannauj, long rows of heavy Mughal cannon stand cold and unused between two vast, tense hosts poised for battle.

dialogue.text: At Kannauj in 1540, Sher Shah Suri broke Humayun’s first empire not by louder guns, but because the Mughal guns never spoke.

i18n.hi: १५४० के कन्नौज में शेरशाह सूरी ने हुमायूँ की पहली सल्तनत को ज़्यादा गोलों से नहीं, बल्कि मुग़ल तोपों की खामोशी से तोड़ा

panels.shot: slow push-in on Humayun at a balcony in Delhi, dusk light, distant campfires beyond the Yamuna
panels.action: Humayun at Chausa stands on a fort balcony in Delhi, cloaked and thoughtful, looking out over the Yamuna towards dim Afghan campfires flickering on the horizon.

dialogue.text: Two years before Kannauj, on the banks of the Ganges at Chausa, Humayun had already felt Sher Shah’s hand close around his young empire.

i18n.hi: कन्नौज से दो साल पहले, गंगा किनारे चौसा में, हुमायूँ ने पहली बार शेरशाह की पकड़ अपने नौजवान साम्राज्य पर महसूस की

panels.shot: low-angle mid-shot of Humayun in a campaign tent, maps spread out, brothers’ names marked, a single lamp casting sharp shadows
panels.action: Inside a campaign tent, Humayun at Chausa leans over a map of Hindustan, his brothers’ names inked at Kabul, Lahore and Kandahar, while a lone lamp throws long, uneasy shadows.

dialogue.text: The Timurid prince ruled Delhi and Agra, yet his power was a net of sand: brothers held frontier thrones, amirs guarded their own fortunes, and Sher Shah watched every split.

i18n.hi: तैमूरी शहज़ादा दिल्ली–आगरा का बादशाह था, पर उसकी ताक़त रेत का जाल थी: भाई सरहदों पर बादशाह, अमीर अपनी दौलत के रखवाले, और शेरशाह हर दरार पर नज़र

panels.shot: wide tracking shot along the Grand Trunk road under construction, laborers, officers, milestones, caravans
panels.action: A long, straight road cuts across green fields, lined with fresh milestones and shady trees, as Afghan supervisors direct laborers and caravans move under watchful horsemen.

dialogue.text: Meanwhile in Bihar and Bengal, Farid Khan, now Sher Shah, stitched his own state: roads, sarais, ferries and strongholds built with care, for war that would move like wind.

i18n.hi: उधर बिहार–बंगाल में फ़रीद ख़ान, जो अब शेरशाह था, अपना सूबा बुन रहा था: सड़कें, सराय, घाट और किले, सब सोच‑समझकर, ताकि जंग तूफ़ान की तरह चले

panels.shot: medium shot inside Sher Shah’s council tent from behind his shoulder, maps of the Ganges plain, arrows toward Agra and Delhi
panels.action: From behind a seated Afghan ruler’s shoulder, we see a map of the Ganges plain spread on a low table, with bold arrows drawn towards Agra and Delhi and tiny forts marked along rivers.

dialogue.text: Abbas Khan Sarwani tells how Sher Shah measured distances, counted ferries and fords, and planned to cut Humayun from his own heartland with speed, not weight alone.

i18n.hi: अब्बास ख़ान सरवानी लिखते हैं कि शेरशाह खुद फासले नापता, घाट–पुल गिनता, और सोचता कि सिर्फ़ ताक़त नहीं, रफ़्तार से हुमायूँ को उसके दिल से काट देगा

panels.shot: dramatic side-shot of night at Chausa, Humayun’s camp tents stretching along the Ganges, storm clouds gathering
panels.action: Under brooding storm clouds by the Ganges at Chausa, long lines of Mughal tents stretch along the bank as watch-fires burn low and sentries pace, their silhouettes tense against the river.

dialogue.text: At Chausa in 1539, Humayun’s army lay heavy and unwary by the river, as Sher Shah crossed in the dark and struck at dawn, driving the Mughals into the Ganges’ flood.

i18n.hi: १५३९ के चौसा में, हुमायूँ की फौज गंगा किनारे भारी, बेफ़िक्र पड़ी थी, जब शेरशाह रात के अंधेरे में पार उतरा और सुबह की नमाज़ पर धावा बोलकर मुग़लों को गंगा की लहरों में धकेल दिया

panels.shot: close-up on a soaked, exhausted Humayun on a small boat, river behind him crowded with men and horses
panels.action: Humayun at Chausa, drenched and exhausted, clutches the side of a small boat as behind him the broad river is choked with struggling men, animals and scattered gear.

dialogue.text: He escaped across the water with his life, his army broken. Sher Shah took the title of king, but the struggle for Hindustan was not yet ended.

i18n.hi: वो किसी तरह पार निकल आया, जान तो बच गई, पर फ़ौज बिखर गई; शेरशाह ने बादशाह का ख़िताब लिया, पर हिंदुस्तान की लड़ाई अभी खत्म नहीं हुई थी

panels.shot: wide shot inside the Diwan hall at Agra, Humayun on the throne, nobles divided in clusters, messengers arriving
panels.action: In the audience hall at Agra, Humayun at Chausa sits on the throne as groups of nobles whisper in separate clusters, while dust-covered messengers arrive from the east and north with sealed letters.

dialogue.text: After Chausa, he still held Agra and Delhi. Yet family letters from Kabul and Lahore carried cold words, and Mughal chroniclers would later speak of brothers who measured every risk in their own coin.

i18n.hi: चौसा के बाद भी उसके पास आगरा और दिल्ली थे; मगर काबुल–लाहौर से आती घरेलू चिट्ठियाँ ठंडी थीं, और मुग़ल इतिहासकार बाद में लिखेंगे कि भाई हर ख़तरे को अपनी जेब से तौलते रहे

panels.shot: medium close-up of Humayun reading a letter, face conflicted, one hand tightening on the scroll
panels.action: Humayun at Chausa sits alone, reading a letter with a troubled gaze, his fingers tightening around the scroll as the lamp flame quivers beside him.

dialogue.speaker: Humayun at Chausa
dialogue.text: So Kamran will not bring all his strength… even now.

i18n.hi: तो कमरान आज भी पूरी ताक़त नहीं भेजेगा…

panels.shot: wide aerial shot of both armies maneuvering along the Ganges between Kannauj and Bilgram, dust clouds pluming
panels.action: From high above, two great columns move along opposite banks of the Ganges near Kannauj and Bilgram, dust rising as they shift and countermarch, probing for a place to cross.

dialogue.text: Through late 1539 and early 1540, Humayun and Sher Shah shadowed each other along the Ganges. Each sought ground that would feed his men, guard his flanks, and trap his rival.

i18n.hi: १५३९ के आख़िर से १५४० की शुरुआत तक हुमायूँ और शेरशाह गंगा के साथ‑साथ चलते रहे; दोनों ऐसी ज़मीन ढूँढ रहे थे जो फौज को खिलाए, पंख बचाए और दुश्मन को फंसाए

panels.shot: ground-level shot of the Mughal artillery park being positioned, massive cannon dragged by oxen, engineers pointing
panels.action: On a flat plain near Kannauj, teams of oxen heave as Mughal gunners and engineers haul massive bronze cannon into a long line, bracing their wheels and eyeing the distant tree line.

dialogue.text: By May 1540, near Kannauj and Bilgram, Humayun anchored his hope in artillery. Mirza Haidar would later write that cannon and firearms stood ready, a wall of metal on the plain.

i18n.hi: १५४० के मई में, कन्नौज–बिलग्राम के पास, हुमायूँ ने अपनी उम्मीद तोपख़ाने पर टिका दी; मिर्ज़ा हैदर बाद में लिखेगा कि तोपें और बंदूकें मैदान में लोहे की दीवार बनकर खड़ी थीं

panels.shot: medium shot of Sher Shah on horseback on a low rise, observing the Mughal camp through the heat haze
panels.action: Sher Shah, an older Afghan leader on horseback, sits on a low ridge, calmly studying the Mughal lines shimmering in the heat, with officers gathered at his side pointing and conferring.

dialogue.text: Across the field, Sher Shah watched those guns and the river at their back. Sarwani says he chose his ground, planned his approach, and trusted his men’s speed more than weight of shot.

i18n.hi: सामने के मोर्चे पर शेरशाह उन तोपों को देख रहा था और पीठ पर बहती नदी को; सरवानी कहते हैं उसने ज़मीन चुनी, रास्ता तय किया, और गोलों से ज़्यादा अपने सिपाहियों की रफ़्तार पर भरोसा किया

panels.shot: tight shot from behind Humayun as he surveys his line of guns and cavalry, morning mist lifting
panels.action: In the pale morning mist, Humayun at Chausa, seen from behind, gazes over the long line of cannon and cavalry stretching across the field, his standard fluttering at the center.

dialogue.speaker: Humayun at Chausa
dialogue.text: We will let the guns break them, then ride them down.

i18n.hi: पहले तोपें इन्हें तोड़ेंगी, फिर हम घोड़ों से कुचल देंगे

panels.shot: wide dynamic shot of Afghan forces advancing in ordered divisions, some slipping toward the flanks, dust swirling
panels.action: Afghan horse and foot advance in ordered blocks across the plain, some columns angling toward the Mughal flanks as dust swirls around their banners and drums.

dialogue.text: On 17 May, Sher Shah’s army moved. Afghan chroniclers describe divisions sent to press the Mughal front, others to feel for their sides, seeking to break the line before the guns could speak.

i18n.hi: १७ मई को शेरशाह की फौज चली; अफ़गान इतिहासकार लिखते हैं कि कुछ दस्ता सामने से दबाने भेजे, कुछ बाएँ–दाएँ टटोलने, ताकि पंक्ति तोड़ दें, इससे पहले कि तोपें बोलें

panels.shot: medium shot of Mughal gunners at their pieces, fuses ready, but officers looking back toward the command tent, uncertain
panels.action: Mughal gunners stand by their cannon with fuses in hand, but their eyes are turned toward the distant royal pavilion, waiting, while officers argue and point in different directions.

dialogue.text: Mirza Haidar records that the cannon and matchlocks were not discharged. Whether from confusion, fear of hitting their own, or orders never given, the thunder stayed locked in iron.

i18n.hi: मिर्ज़ा हैदर लिखते हैं कि न तोप चली, न बंदूक; न जाने गड़बड़ी से, अपने ही मरने के डर से, या हुक्म ही न आने से, गरज लोहे के सीने में बंद रही

panels.shot: chaotic wide shot of the Mughal center as Afghan attack hits, cavalry wheeling, dust blinding, the gun line beginning to buckle
panels.action: As Afghan troops crash into the Mughal center, horsemen wheel and collide in a storm of dust, while the long line of silent cannon wavers and gaps appear where men fall back in disorder.

dialogue.text: Without the planned hail of shot, Sher Shah’s charge bit deep into the Mughal center. The line that had been drawn around the guns became a tangle of men seeking to save themselves.

i18n.hi: जब तयशुदा गोलों की बारिश नहीं हुई, तो शेरशाह का धावा मुग़ल बीचोंबीच धँस गया; तोपों के चारों तरफ बनाई गई लकीर टूटकर ऐसे बिखरी कि हर आदमी बस अपनी जान बचाने लगा

panels.shot: medium close-up of Humayun amid fleeing troops, trying to rally them, his horse rearing slightly
panels.action: Humayun at Chausa, mounted amid a stream of fleeing soldiers, raises his arm and shouts, his horse half-rearing as men rush past him toward the river.

dialogue.speaker: Humayun at Chausa
dialogue.text: Hold the line! Face them—do not throw away the field!

i18n.hi: पंक्ति थामो! सामने देखो—मैदान यूँ मत फेंको!

panels.shot: wide shot toward the Ganges, Mughal camp followers and soldiers crowding toward the river, Afghan forces pressing in the distance
panels.action: The Ganges gleams in the distance as streams of Mughal camp followers, elephants and soldiers pour toward its banks, while far behind them Afghan troops advance steadily across the abandoned field.

dialogue.text: But the memory of Chausa clung to the men. With the river once more at their backs and the Afghan attack unbroken, many thought of escape before thought of standing.

i18n.hi: पर चौसा की याद इनके दिलों से चिपकी थी; पीछे फिर से नदी, सामने अफ़गान हमला, तो बहुतों के दिमाग़ में खड़ा होने से पहले भागने का ख़्याल आया

panels.shot: long shot of Sher Shah’s camp after the battle, Mughal standards stacked, captured guns lined up, officers inspecting
panels.action: After the battle, in Sher Shah’s camp, Mughal standards lie stacked and heavy cannon stand in captured rows as Afghan officers walk between them, studying the great bronze mouths that never fired.

dialogue.text: Kannauj completed what Chausa began. Humayun’s army had broken again; his guns were trophies, his road to Delhi and Agra closed by Sher Shah’s new authority.

i18n.hi: कन्नौज ने चौसा की कहानी पूरी कर दी; हुमायूँ की फौज फिर टूट गई, उसकी तोपें लूट की निशानी बनीं, और दिल्ली–आगरा का रास्ता अब शेरशाह की मुहर से बंद हो गया

panels.shot: somber mid-shot of Humayun in a small boat on a broad river again, this time more composed, looking back toward the receding plains
panels.action: Humayun at Chausa sits more composed in a riverboat gliding downstream, his gaze fixed on the fading plains behind, where distant smoke marks the lost heartland.

dialogue.text: From the Ganges plain he turned away, into years of wandering in Sindh’s deserts, then to Persia and Afghanistan, a king without a kingdom seeking allies and another chance.

i18n.hi: वो गंगा की मैदानी दुनिया से मुड़कर सिंध के रेगिस्तानों में भटकता रहा, फिर फ़ारस और अफ़ग़ानिस्तान, एक बिन तख़्त का बादशाह, जो हमसफ़र और दूसरा मौक़ा ढूँढता रहा

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of Sher Shah inspecting a new sarai on the Grand Trunk road, with road, trees, and travelers
panels.action: Sher Shah rides past a freshly built sarai along a broad straight road, its brick arches facing a steady line of travelers—merchants, soldiers and peasants—moving under newly planted trees.

dialogue.text: In Delhi and along the old Uttarapatha, Sher Shah set his order: revenues measured, coins reformed, roads stitched and sarais raised, policies the later Mughals would adopt when they returned.

i18n.hi: दिल्ली और पुराने उत्तरापथ पर शेरशाह ने अपना निज़ाम बैठाया: लगान नापा, सिक्के सुधारे, सड़कें जोड़ीं और सरायें खड़ी कीं—वे ही चालें जिन्हें लौटकर आने वाले मुग़ल अपनाएँगे

panels.shot: split composition: on one side, silent cannon at Kannauj; on the other, a later Mughal official measuring fields with a rope
panels.action: The scene divides: on one side, an abandoned cannon at Kannauj rusts on the plain; on the other, years later, a Mughal official measures a field with a rope while a peasant watches.

dialogue.text: Irfan Habib and others trace how Sher Shah’s revenue and road systems outlived his dynasty, woven into Akbar’s empire—Kannauj’s defeat shaping the rules of the kingdom that would follow.

i18n.hi: इर्फ़ान हबीब व दूसरे बताते हैं कि शेरशाह की लगान और सड़क का सिस्टम उसकी नस्ल से भी ज़्यादा जिया, अकबर की सल्तनत में घुल गया—कन्नौज की हार ने आने वाले राज्य के क़ायदे लिखे

panels.shot: intimate close-up on an older Humayun’s face (hint of age), eyes reflecting both hardship and resolve, background blurred
panels.action: In a later moment, an older Humayun at Chausa gazes ahead, his face lined by exile, his eyes carrying both loss and the quiet fire of one who has walked back from defeat.

dialogue.text: When Humayun returned years later with Persian aid, he walked again over plains where his guns had once kept their silence. Kannauj remained in his memory as the price of divided command.

i18n.hi: सालों बाद जब हुमायूँ फ़ारसी मदद के साथ लौटा, तो फिर उन मैदानों से गुज़रा जहाँ उसकी तोपें कभी चुप रही थीं; कन्नौज उसकी याद में बँटा हुआ फ़रमान होने की कीमत बनकर रहा

panels.shot: final contemplative wide shot of the empty Kannauj field at sunset, faint outlines of old trenches and gun positions in the grass
panels.action: At sunset, the quiet field near Kannauj lies empty, faint traces of old trenches and gun ruts just visible in the grass as the Ganges gleams far away under a red sky.

dialogue.text: On that plain, a weapon unused weighed as heavily as any blow struck. Kannauj reminds us that empires can fall not only to enemy steel, but to silence, hesitation and roads left open to another’s design.

i18n.hi: उस मैदान पर, जो हथियार चला ही नहीं, उसका बोझ भी चलाए गए वार जितना भारी था; कन्नौज याद दिलाता है कि सल्तनतें सिर्फ़ दुश्मन की तलवार से नहीं, खामोशी, झिझक और खुली छोड़ दी गई राहों से भी गिरती हैं

subtitle_i18n.en: When cannon kept their silence, an empire lost its voice
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब तोपें चुप रहीं, साम्राज्य की आवाज़ बुझ गई
